answer.rationale: Degradation began after the release 2 hours ago, is confined to the primary region (pointing at the build, not infrastructure), and memory_b1 records rollback cleanly clearing a prior checkout error spike with no customer impact and no write loss — critical at settlement peak. I verify memory_b1 (rollback safety/write-preservation) and memory_b2 (confirms recent gating history, to calibrate how likely this release escaped detection). Regional failover is the second-best option but slower and risks write divergence during peak; capacity and replicas don't fit a write-path regression. If verification shows b1's rollback had caveats (e.g., schema incompatibility), I'd fall back to regional failover. Rollback is standard and reversible, so I stage it as a guarded step with immediate health checks rather than assuming the release is certainly the cause — the peak-traffic correlation is a confound I can't fully rule out.
